title: Angkor Wat
summary: Angkor Wat, near Siem Reap in Cambodia, is the state temple of the Khmer king Suryavarman II, built from 1113 and completed after his death about 1150. A three-level stepped pyramid topped by five towers, with a central shrine 65 m high, it was dedicated to Vishnu. It is the largest and most important monument at Angkor.

uncertainty.note: Start is the beginning of Suryavarman II's reign, 1113, from which the MIT Libraries record dates creation (1113 to ca. 1150); the temple was completed after his death c. 1150. End is the present: it is a living monument and UNESCO property.

phases.description: Built as a royal temple-mountain by Suryavarman II (r. 1113-1150) but not completed until after his death, c. 1150.

Stands as a continuously known monument; in the 16th century Buddhist sculptures were placed in the shrines and the gold Vishnu statue was removed (German Angkor Imagery Project). Restoration works at Angkor ran from 1907 to 1992 (UNESCO).

reviewer_note: Shape stepped_pyramid (three levels with a quincunx of towers). Least sure of the base size: 187 x 215 m is the outer gallery per Notre Dame and is printed in parentheses in the MIT record next to the 1025 x 802 m outer wall, so the MIT figure's meaning is ambiguous; I used Notre Dame for the pyramid-level plan and MIT for the enclosure. The 65 m height is in the MIT record and is repeated by the German Angkor Imagery Project, a non-institutional source (class other), which is the one spotcheck can read. The MIT figures (1025 x 802, 60 x 60, 65 m) sit in the page's embedded metadata JSON, which spotcheck strips; I confirmed them by reading the raw page. The 'intact' phase glosses over 16th-century changes and modern restoration, noted in the description only. UNESCO's points for property 668 are not at the temple, so coordinates come from OpenStreetMap.
